hitl_conditions: Alerts issued when predicted risk exceeds predefined thresholds, at graded severity with escalation pathways tied to organisational roles; decision-makers then evaluate and select twin-simulated mitigation strategies. Automation versus human authority is not explicitly discussed.
key_finding: Simulated Malaysian supply chain CDEWS: RNN and graph-based risk forecasting on fused multimodal data plus a supply chain digital twin for what-if mitigation analysis raised disruption lead time from 8–12 h to 64–72 h and cut logistics downtime roughly one-third, stockout risk and recovery duration in three flood/rainfall scenarios.

quotes.text: The digital twin mirrors the evolving state of the physical supply chain and allows “what-if” analysis under alternative intervention policies, such as rerouting shipments, reallocating inventory, or activating backup suppliers.
CDEWS-enabled performance was evaluated by activating multimodal data fusion, predictive risk modelling, and digital twin–based simulation as described in Section 3.

The system models supply chains as interconnected networks of nodes and links, where nodes represent ports, warehouses, factories, suppliers, and distribution centres, and links represent transport and information flows.

Recurrent neural networks are employed to capture temporal dependencies in climate and operational time series, while graph-based models represent the structural dependencies within supply chain networks [6].

Finally, a decision support and governance layer translates predictive outputs into interpretable alerts, recommendations, and escalation pathways aligned with organisational roles and regulatory requirements.
Digital twin–based simulation allows decision-makers to evaluate alternative recovery strategies and select those that minimise downtime and resource strain.
